# CRC32

**Class** · `ironwood.util.zip.CRC32`

```java
public class CRC32
```

Computes the CRC-32 checksum of a byte stream: the checksum that ZIP entries and GZIP
members record for their uncompressed bytes (reflected polynomial `0xEDB88320`,
initial and final value `0xFFFFFFFF`).



A new or reset checksum has the value 0. Updates consume bytes in order, so updating
with a range in several pieces gives the same value as one update with the whole range.
[`getValue()`](#member-getValue-28--29-) only reads the current value; further updates continue from it.
Updates allocate nothing and borrow their array only for the duration of the call.



This first slice of the Java `java.util.zip.CRC32` API omits the
`Checksum` interface and the `ByteBuffer` update. The class is not final:
as in Java, [`update(byte[])`](#member-update-28-byte-5b--5d--29-) delegates to the dynamically selected
[`update(byte[],int,int)`](#member-update-28-byte-5b--5d--2c-int-2c-int-29-), so a subclass that overrides the range update also
observes whole-array updates.

### `update(int)`

```java
public void update(int b)
```

Updates the checksum with one byte: the low eight bits of `b`. Higher bits,
including the sign of a widened negative value, are ignored.

| --- | --- |
